findings.where: KO sentence 25; ontology.translation row 10 (F4, F19, F20); P section 'The mantle', item 'Routing'; ontology.case.statement; ontology.receiving_texts; joins 'translation'; delta.LB_vs_LBA last sentence
findings.finding: The row's one witness-sense act, placing the programme's cloak 'in the archive's routing' as the mantle in its metaphorical sense, has no archive locus. None of the cited claims (PP1691-27, PP1691-26, PP1691-33) mentions the cloak. #1691 defines the metaphorical mantle as a standing that passes between holders, not as a garment. Where #1691 does speak of the cloak, it puts it inside the programme's awarded-title branch and carries it as received. Read that way, F4/F19/F20 belong to an equal-terms branch and are untranslated. The P item repeats the act and attributes it to #1691 ('the winner's cloak among it, "need not be the archive's" (#1691)').
findings.evidence: #1691 Seven branches: 'The program's awarded title | Conferred on each season's winner under the competition's selection procedure, with a symbolic cloak and ring and one million dirhams'. #1691 Retrieval Instructions: '"The mantle of the Prince of Poets" in its metaphorical sense, a branch's standing as it passes from holder to holder, need not be the archive's.' No occurrence of 'cloak' elsewhere in #1691 (grep).
findings.fix: Translation row 10: 'untranslated: composed as received beside PP1691-12' (receiving_text '—'). S25 becomes: '#1691 carries the cloak within the programme's awarded title, "with a symbolic cloak and ring and one million dirhams"; separately, "the mantle of the Prince of Poets" in its metaphorical sense, "a branch's standing as it passes from holder to holder", "need not be the archive's", while within a Prince of Poets context "the mantle object" names the archive's mantle, "the one branch with a documented computational construction", on the author's ruling: "…reference to the mantle object is reference to the semantic object ive constructed".' findings.where: KO sentence 14; P section 'The titles', item 'Shawqi:' ('his death dated 13 or 14 October 1932'); P open item 1; plan conflict_log (P_coh, sentence 14); field claims F50, F51, F52
findings.finding: The Britannica claims F50–F52 come from a summarising fetch. Direct download returned HTTP 403. Under §3.1 that is not a fetch, and the card snippet (F65) stands as the source's only text. The death-day contest between 14 and 13 October is composed as a P_coh conflict, carried on the compression and posed as an open question, but it rests only on F52. F65 gives the years alone. The exile contest (F46 against F65) is sound. S13's Britannica 'proclaimed' is also sound, because #1691 quotes it (PP1691-09).
findings.evidence: §3.1: 'Extraction reads the saved text only; a summarising fetch is not a fetch … A source that cannot be fetched is recorded as unreachable with the response code, the time and the retries attempted, and its card snippet stands as its only text.' F52 quote_ok 'webfetch'; F65: 'Aḥmad Shawqī: Egyptian poet (1868–1932); … exiled in Spain (1914–19)'.
findings.fix: Mark F50–F52 'unsupported' (not fetched, §3.1); keep F65. S14: 'Wikipedia has him die in Cairo on 14 October 1932 and remain in Andalusia from 1914 until 1920; Britannica's card gives his exile in Spain as "(1914–19)".' P 'Shawqi:' item: 'his exile's end 1919 or 1920'. Open item 1: drop the death date or record that it rests on an unfetched text. S12: take Britannica's wording from F65 ('known as amīr al-shuʿarāʾ ("prince of poets"); pioneer of Arabic poetical drama').

findings.finding: ρ = extends is supported. The witness part of 'mixed' is not. §0.9 sets two conditions for the witness case: the archive 'radically contests the field's ontology' AND supplies an ontology no other source makes available. #1691 contests no branch. It relates the mantle to the others 'by the phrase' and requires that each branch 'keeps its own'. #1656 puts the field's titles and the mantle in one ontology, titles assigned to works, with the mantle object 'a prototype of the other course: an assignment procedure made rigorous'. A reader of the same papers would more likely read equal terms throughout: the mantle is a seventh sense the field lacks, composed as a definition among definitions, the way model collapse's four added senses are. Under that reading nothing needs translating. The only operational effect of the witness label is the unlicensed cloak translation (C1). §10.16 is open for the operator's ruling, and the row already flags this, so the label is recorded as disagreed, not as a defect in the loci (all twelve case loci are verbatim).
findings.evidence: §0.9: 'Where the archive radically contests the field's ontology and supplies an ontology no other source makes available, the archive's ontology rules.' #1691 Relations: 'The archive's mantle shares the English phrase with all of these and is related to them by the phrase.' #1656 preface: 'A mantle has always been a constructed semantic object: a title assigned to a work by a circle, a crowd or a critic … This packet is a prototype of the other course: an assignment procedure made rigorous and inspectable'.
findings.fix: Record the case as equal terms (ρ = extends), or keep 'mixed' with this reading as a recorded alternative beside ontology.rho.alternative and send both to the operator under §10.16. Under either reading, F4/F19/F20 stay untranslated (C1).

findings.where: KO sentence 41; P section 'Identify, then judge', item 'State:'
findings.finding: The 29e round's 'SINGULAR CLAIM PLAUSIBLE' is carried without the limits #1656 attaches to it. In a ROUND a judgment is provisional, and the term itself means the rival field 'has not been searched enough to decide'. The same paragraph also states the round's own limits. Without these limits the judgment reads at more than its force. The ledger quote PP1656-12 stops before them. This is the one place where the KO's non-judging (checked separately, C16) is weakened.
findings.evidence: #1656 §14.2: 'SINGULAR CLAIM PLAUSIBLE, the magnitude is substantial and the rival field has not been searched enough to decide … in a ROUND it is provisional'. #1656 A.6: 'Its loci check against the seated texts, and its Leaves of Grass is cited in general terms only.'
findings.fix: Extract #1656 §14.2's definition and the A.6 limit into the ledger. S41: '…returned "SINGULAR CLAIM PLAUSIBLE for the Prince of Poets", which #1656 defines as "the magnitude is substantial and the rival field has not been searched enough to decide", provisional in a ROUND, its Leaves of Grass "cited in general terms only"…'.

findings.where: Additional check (#1691 §Two operations): KO and P as a whole
findings.finding: Passes, with one weak point. The KO identifies the title and leaves judgment where the archive places it. S39–S44 say where and how a claim is judged (#1651, #1656) and give the dataset's recorded state. S3 and S34 keep the operations apart. Open item 4 says the composition does not judge. No sentence assesses the poem. The one weak point is S41's force (C6). S29 quotes #1651's 'the legitimate continuation', attributed and at the source's own stipulative modality. Under N_c that is correct, and the tension with #1651's own open question ('whether … legitimately founds') is the source's.
findings.evidence: #1691: 'Identifying the mantle and judging whether a work bears it are separate operations.' P open item 4: 'this composition identifies the title and does not judge it (#1691)'.

findings.finding:
Checks run that passed:
- Every quoted span in KO sentences 1–49 and the P items appears in a cited ledger quote. The one exception is the address string in S48, which is a query, not a quote.
- All cited ids exist in the ledgers.
- All 113 archive quotes are found verbatim in their seated texts (AXN-<hex> via registry; #1691 = 0701).
- All twelve case loci are verbatim.
- The translation table holds every field claim (F1–F65) exactly once, each received quote verbatim from field.json.
- C_ex against the ledger is complete (every ledger claim cited in the KO), and every kernel claim appears on the rail.
- P body: about 297 words, within the 350-word bound.
- The T and T2 paste hashes match the row, the T claims are verbatim against the paste, and the T2 card rail matches the paste's eight cards.
- The four contradicts_primary loci are composed as marked (S37, S38).

summary: ρ = extends is supported, and the composition is faithful to its ledgers almost throughout: quotes are verbatim, the translation is complete and verbatim, coverage and kernels are complete. The KO identifies the title and does not judge it. Three must-fix findings: (1) the one witness-sense act, translating the programme's cloak as the metaphorical mantle, has no archive locus, since #1691 puts the cloak in the awarded-title branch as received; (2) delta.T2 says ʿAmʿaq's 1148 death date is not composed, but T2's heading composes it; (3) the Shawqi death-day contest and its open question rest only on Britannica text from a summarising fetch, which §3.1 rules out. I do not agree with the 'mixed' case reading: #1691 contests no branch, so a reader of the same papers would more likely read equal terms throughout.
